subject: Traffic signalization: concurrency & token-shape confirmation for POC
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@clearstream.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Traffic signalization: concurrency & token-shape confirmation for POC

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a small ask so we can finalize the trial scope: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use: multi-turn assistant for customer support (2–4 turns typical).
- Model shape: mix of short prompts (50–200 tokens in) and longer completions (~300–600 tokens out).
- Current baseline RPS: ~7 sustained; observed short bursts up to ~120–160 RPS lasting 60–180s during peak hours.
- Concurrency footprint: ~30–60 concurrent user sessions during peak.

Our asks to size the POC properly
1) Can you share a short sample of traffic (CSV export or aggregated histogram) with columns: timestamp, call_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, caller_region? A CSV stub is perfect.
2) Confirm expected P95 latency SLO (what would you consider acceptable for the pilot?).
3) Who on ClearStream will own telemetry/ops access for the test (email + Slack handle)?
4) Any redlines on data retention/PII we should know about?

What we propose next (draft POC plan)
- 2-week pilot window (we can flex dates) with staged ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% of baseline RPS.
- Success criteria: stability at 100% baseline + handling observed burst profile without >5% error/failures, p95 generation latency target to be agreed.
- Redwood owners: Soojin (eng) for runtime, Ben (sales) for contracting/ops.

I attached our lightweight POC checklist to speed approvals. If you can drop the traffic sample and any telemetry contact, I’ll align Soojin and get a precise test harness scheduled.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_poc_checklist.pdf (PDF)]

From: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@clearstream.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: security@clearstream.ai
Date: Sat, 04 Mar 2028 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Traffic signalization: concurrency & token-shape confirmation for POC

Marcus — appreciate the clear recap. Attached a one-day sample export and an internal note from infra. High-level answers below: 

Quick numbers (sample day, PST)
- Average tokens_in: 120
- Average tokens_out: 410
- Median conversation turns: 3
- Baseline RPS (business hours): 6–8 sustained
- Observed peak bursts: 140–160 RPS for 90–150s windows (usually M/W 11:00–11:15 PST)
- Typical concurrency: 28–55 sessions (varies by region)

Telemetry & owners
- Ops owner: Daniel Park <daniel.park@clearstream.ai> (cc’d on infra note we attached)
- Security contact: security@clearstream.ai (cc’d) — SOC2 evidence requests are welcome; we’ll route through them.

PII / retention
- We can produce an anonymized sample (no raw user IDs). Production retention policy is 30 days; can work with shorter retention for the pilot if required.

Notes: we’re comfortable with Redwood running a controlled synthetic ramp against a test cluster. Please confirm what minimal IAM/endpoint access you need and whether you require a dedicated pool for the trial.

Attachments: clearstream_traffic_sample.csv (first 1,000 rows) and infra_note_for_poc.txt

Best,
Emily Zhou
Head of Product — ClearStream AI
[Attachment: clearstream_traffic_sample.csv (CSV)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@clearstream.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Traffic signalization: concurrency & token-shape confirmation for POC

Thanks Emily — that sample is exactly what we needed. Quick follow-up with a proposed concrete pilot plan so you can circulate internally: 

Proposed pilot (draft)
- Window: 2 weeks between Mar 13 and Mar 27 (flexible).
- Ramp plan: Day 1–2: 10% baseline synthetic; Day 3–5: 50%; Day 6–end: 100% baseline plus 2 scheduled burst windows to reproduce 140–160 RPS for ~2 minutes each.
- Success criteria (example)
  - Stability: error rate (5xx) <= 0.5% over 24h windows during 100% baseline
  - Performance: p95 generation latency < 350ms (subject to model selection)
  - Functional: no regressions on a provided eval prompt set (we’ll sync on 10–20 prompts)
- Measurement approach: Redwood will run synthetic replay against a test endpoint and also accept sampled production traffic if ClearStream prefers (we can sign an NDA-addendum).

Owners & asks
- Redwood runtime lead: Soojin Lee (soojin.lee@redwood.com) — will coordinate test harness and observability hooks.
- Commercial: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.com) — will finalize trial terms and any short-term credits.
- ClearStream: please confirm Daniel Park as the telemetry owner and provide an IAM role or short-lived token for test replay.

Immediate next steps
1) ClearStream: confirm telemetry owner and share minimal access (sample CSV already received — thank you).
2) Red: Soojin to propose test endpoints and a synthetic load script by EOD Tue.
3) Ben & Emily: finalize trial contract addendum and dates.

Linking the HubSpot record for the deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/clearstream-ai/CS-4721

If that looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff with engineering next week.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@clearstream.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Mar 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Traffic signalization: concurrency & token-shape confirmation for POC

Hi Emily / Marcus — looping in a few technical checks so we size the runtime correctly: 

Technical clarifications
- Token distribution: the CSV shows a long tail of ~15% of calls producing >900 tokens_out. Please confirm whether those are expected (e.g., long transcripts) or if we should treat them as outliers for the pilot.
- Concurrency vs session: are sessions sticky to a user (same session_id across multiple calls) or is each request independent? Stickiness changes KV cache hit rates and memory sizing.
- Burst pattern: we’ll schedule two synthetic bursts that mirror the timestamps in your sample; if you can provide a 5-minute trace for a representative burst window that includes request arrival timestamps that helps with shaping the replay.

What we will provision for the pilot (initial plan)
- Dedicated test pool sized for 2x observed peak tokens-per-second (conservative) plus continuous KV cache to simulate session stickiness.
- Observability: p50/p95/p99, error classification, and token-cost breakdown per call. We’ll expose a temporary dashboard link during the run.

Small asks to proceed
1) A 5-minute raw trace (anonymized) from one peak burst window (timestamps + session_id + tokens_in/tokens_out).
2) Confirmation on whether ClearStream wants us to include prefix/KV caching behavior in the test. If yes, provide typical session length in turns.

I can have a load script and a runbook (endpoints + test harness) ready by EOD Wed once we have the 5-min trace.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee | Runtime Lead, Redwood Inference
[Note: attaching runbook after we sync; no PII requested beyond session_id anonymization]
